key_fields.sql: select z.borough, count(*) as touches from lake.trips t join ops.zones z on z.locationid = t.pulocationid or z.locationid = t.dolocationid group by z.borough order by z.borough

value.bottleneck: The BLOCKWISE_NL_JOIN (node 8) performs a nested-loop join over 495,833 trips rows and 265 zones rows with an OR join condition (PULocationID OR DOLocationID), preventing hash-join optimization and likely executing ~130M comparisons.

hypotheses.claim: The OR join condition forces a nested-loop join instead of a hash join; rewriting as a UNION ALL of two separate equi-joins (one on PULocationID, one on DOLocationID) followed by aggregation would enable hash joins and reduce comparisons to ~1M.
Neither trips.PULocationID nor trips.DOLocationID has an index; creating a hash index or sorting trips on both columns would allow a merge join or hash join on each key individually.
The blockwise nested-loop join materializes the full cross-product for the OR condition; pushing a bloom filter or pre-filtering zones into the scan could reduce the inner-loop iterations.
